about.title: Soledad Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Soledad residents rely on a limited number of local clinics and, for more serious care, hospitals outside Monterey County's smaller towns. California law puts real conditions on these claims — including notice deadlines and expert review requirements — which makes early guidance valuable. We handle medical malpractice cases and do not guarantee any result; we review medical records, evaluate whether the care fell below the accepted standard, and explain your options. There's no cost to start the conversation, and we only get paid if your case results in a recovery. If a medical experience in Soledad left you with new or worsened harm, it's worth understanding your rights before time limits close in.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Wait

items.title: Strict, Layered Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims within one year of discovering the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. A 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider is also required, so acting early matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, California cases typically need a qualified medical expert to show the care fell below the accepted standard. Our team can help arrange that kind of review.

items.title: Damages Caps Apply, But They Rise Over Time
items.desc: California law caps non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, though that cap increases annually under current rules. Understanding how the cap applies to your situation is something we can walk through with you.

items.question: I think a Soledad clinic missed something on my test results — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the outcome was poor. We can review your records to see whether the facts support a claim.

items.question: How much time do I have to bring a claim after treatment in Soledad?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the date of the injury, whichever comes first. There's also a required 90-day notice period before filing suit, so it helps to start the process well before any deadline approaches.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our initial case review is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we're only paid if your case results in a recovery. There's no obligation to move forward after the initial conversation.
